choice: Managing overlapping tasks vs executing tasks at the same time.
example: One cook can alternate tasks; several cooks can work simultaneously.

choice: Repeated waiting requests vs a persistent two-way connection.
example: Use message direction, frequency, and reconnect behavior to choose.

choice: Process accumulated records together vs process a continuing flow.
example: Nightly sales reports favor batches; live fraud signals need timely updates.

choice: Requests depend on server-local session state vs portable request context.
example: With an external session store, another app server can handle the next request.

choice: Reads reflect completed writes vs replicas converge after writes stop and communication recovers.
example: Profile display may tolerate lag; stock reservation needs an explicit correctness rule.

choice: The cache loads missed reads vs the cache layer persists writes synchronously.
example: A product cache can load read misses and synchronously persist writes; these policies can be combined.

choice: Sender initiates delivery vs receiver requests updates.
example: A webhook pushes payment news; polling repeatedly asks for it.

choice: Resource-oriented interfaces vs calling defined operations.
example: Use resource reads for products; typed service operations can reserve inventory.

choice: Caller waits for completion vs completion is decoupled from the initiating call.
example: Queued email can finish after the order confirmation.

choice: Time for one operation vs operations completed per unit time.
example: More counters can serve more customers without shortening each individual checkout.
